message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on a decorative owl figure made of mixed natural materials. The likely classification is 4420.90 (wooden statuettes and other ornaments), or 4602 (basketware), or 9505 (festive articles), or 6702/0604 (artificial flowers and foliage).

I recall a ruling on a similar owl that fell under 4414 or 4420. Here the materials are sisal, cattails, straw, birch, and banana leaf, all vegetable materials. Under 4602 ("basketwork, wickerwork and other articles made directly to shape from plaiting materials") the owl would not qualify, since it is built on a Styrofoam form. Heading 4420 covers wooden statuettes and ornaments, but wood does not predominate here. Heading 9505 covers festive articles and applies only if the item is for a specific holiday, and nothing in the description indicates one. That leaves 4420 as a candidate, but also 6702 and 9989 as alternatives.

The remaining option is a residual heading such as 9602 or 4421. I think the ruling may have placed it in 4602.19 or 4421. By essential character, the vegetable materials cover the figure, and the wood is only birch slices and a twig. A decorative figure of mixed vegetable material that is not wood would most likely go in 4602.19 or 9505.90. Because the item is not holiday-specific, I will go with 4420.19 or 4420.90. The 4420.90 subheading, "Wood marquetry... statuettes and other ornaments, of wood," has a statistical suffix of 4420.90.8000 or 4420.90.8000 for other. Alternatively, the figure may be classified as an "other" article of vegetable materials in 1404.90. I'll choose 4420.90.8000.

{"hts_code": "4420.90.8000", "reason": "A decorative owl figure whose surface is covered in natural vegetable materials including birch twig slices, perched on a wooden twig, is treated as a statuette or ornament of wood under heading 4420, in the residual 'other' subheading."}
